jobs.title: AVP, Delivery Excellence & Transformation
jobs.description:
The AVP, Delivery Excellence & Transformation sets the strategy for how Technology plans, resources and delivers work, bringing together program and project management, Agile practices and AI-enabled transformation to improve predictability and business outcomes. The role aligns quarterly delivery planning with enterprise planning, funding and governance. Accountabilities span development of delivery leaders and professionals, and ownership of delivery platforms, workforce planning, internal and external resource allocation, and strategic staffing and delivery partnerships.

The AVP leads enterprise-wide delivery transformation, defining and implementing an AI-enabled delivery model that simplifies processes, redefines roles and controls, and embeds new ways of working. The mandate is to remove unnecessary complexity and deliver measurable business outcomes through effective AI adoption.

What You Will Do

Lead program and project management, Scrum Master and Agile Coaching practices, setting standards and driving continuous improvement across traditional and Agile delivery.
Develop delivery leaders and professionals through career pathways, coaching and practical AI skills.
Align quarterly delivery planning, including PI Planning and Big Room Planning, with enterprise priorities, funding and governance; partner with platform leaders to address dependencies, readiness gaps and prioritization decisions. Partner with business, technology and corporate leaders to clarify accountabilities and align delivery practices with enterprise requirements.
Lead enterprise-wide adoption of the AI-enabled delivery model, challenging established practices, eliminating low-value work and simplifying processes, roles and controls; build commitment to change and align adoption with enterprise standards.
Own delivery tools for project and resource tracking, ensuring reliable data and integrated, automated reporting.
Establish delivery performance measures and validate AI benefits against baselines, using evidence to guide improvement and investment decisions.
Own Technology workforce planning, talent intake and internal and external resource allocation, aligning skills and capacity with funded demand.
Manage Engineering operating expense forecasts and savings commitments, translating realized productivity gains into workforce and sourcing decisions.
Manage strategic staffing and delivery partnerships, setting contractual expectations for quality, productivity, AI adoption and security; work with Procurement, Legal and Architecture on commercial terms and remediation.
Challenge the status quo, remove unnecessary complexity and focus on outcomes over process.
Develop people, build commitment to change and lead effective AI adoption.
Exercise sound financial judgment and hold teams and partners accountable for measurable business results.

What You Will Bring

Experience leading Program and Project Management and Agile delivery practices in a complex enterprise, developing leaders and professionals, and driving continuous improvement across traditional and Agile approaches.
Expertise in enterprise and quarterly delivery planning, including aligning priorities, funding, capacity and dependencies; sound judgment in applying project management, SAFe, Scrum and Lean practices to business needs.
Demonstrated success redesigning processes, roles and controls through AI and automation, with practical knowledge of generative and agentic AI adoption and evidence of measurable benefits beyond tool deployment.
Strong workforce planning, resource allocation and financial acumen, including operating expense forecasting, savings realization and management of internal and external technology capacity.
Experience managing strategic technology staffing and delivery partnerships, including sourcing, commercial negotiations, contractual expectations and partner performance.
Experience owning delivery-platform requirements and adoption, establishing reliable data and performance measures, and validating productivity and delivery improvements against baselines.
Proven experience leading enterprise-wide transformation, with strong executive communication and cross-functional influence to build commitment, navigate resistance and sustain adoption. A change-oriented mindset and strong bias for simplifying complexity, challenging the status quo and delivering measurable business outcomes.

This posting represents an existing vacancy within our organization.

We may use artificial intelligence tools as part of our recruitment process to assist in the initial screening of resumes. All hiring decisions, including candidate evaluation, selection, and disposition, are made by human recruiters.

About Us

Canadian Tire Corporation, Limited (“CTC”) is one of Canada’s most admired and trusted companies. With more than 90 Owned Brands, over 1,600 retail locations, financial services, exemplary e-commerce capabilities, and exciting market-leading merchandising strategies. We dream big and work as one to innovate with purpose for our customers at every level of our business, investing in new technologies and products, and doubling down on top talent to drive the company forward. We offer competitive salaries and wages to CTC employees, as well as store discounts, supported learning through our Triangle Learning Academy, Canadian Tire Profit Sharing, and retirement and savings programs for eligible employees. As part of our enhanced flex benefits program, we offer mental health benefits in the amount of $5,000 per year for benefits-eligible employees and their families, including total well-being, and mental health tools and resources for all employees. Join us in helping to make life in Canada better through living and working our Core Values: we are innovators and entrepreneurs at our core, outcomes drive us, inclusion is a must, we are stronger together and we take personal responsibility. It is an especially exciting time to join CTC and its family of companies where career opportunities are wide-ranging! Join us, where there's a place for you here.

Our Commitment to Diversity, Inclusion and Belonging

We are committed to fostering an environment where belonging thrives, and diversity, inclusion and equity are infused into everything we do. We believe in building an organizational culture where people are consistently treated with dignity while respecting individual religion, nationality, gender, race, age, perceived ability, spoken language, sexual orientation, and identification. We are united in our purpose of being here to help make life in Canada better.

Accommodations

We stand firm in our Core Value that inclusion is a must. We welcome and encourage candidates from equity-seeking groups such as people who identify as racialized, Indigenous, 2SLGBTQIA+, women, people with disabilities, and beyond. jobs.title: Director Strategy and Delivery Real World Late Phase
jobs.description:
Description

Director Strategy and Delivery Real World Late Phase

Syneos Health® is a leading fully-integrated life sciences services organization built to accelerate customer success. We partner with innovators at every point across the drug development and commercialization continuum, helping them navigate complexity, anticipate change and accelerate progress.

Our Clinical Solutions team members act with a drug development mindset, applying their years of experience and deep expertise to truly understand customer needs and represent those in the solutions we shape.

Whether you join us in a Functional Service Provider partnership or a Full-Service environment, you’ll collaborate with passionate problem solvers, innovating as a team to help our customers achieve their goals. We are agile and driven to deliver – for one another, our customers, and, most importantly, for those in need.

Discover what your 25,000 future colleagues already know:

Why Syneos Health

We are passionate about developing our people, through career development and progression; supportive and engaged line management; technical and therapeutic area training; peer recognition and total rewards program.
We are committed to building an inclusive culture – where you can authentically be yourself. Central to this is our purpose – Driven to Deliver – which captures the passion of our colleagues to show up each day and shape solutions that have the ability to dramatically impact someone’s life.
We are continuously building the company we all want to work for and our customers want to work with. Why? Because we know that when we bring together smart colleagues from across the world, we can shape the future of healthcare, driving impact for customers and defining the pace of patient progress.

Job Responsibilities

Job Summary

The Director, Strategy & Delivery, Real World Late Phase (RWLP), independently leads customer engagements from pre-award strategy through study delivery. The role combines ownership of study strategy, proposal development and bid defenses with operational and financial oversight of assigned studies, programs and portfolios. The Director partners with Business Development and Medical Strategy to secure new business, support account growth and ensure that proposal commitments translate into achievable delivery plans.

The Director develops practical delivery solutions for non-interventional and interventional late-phase research, including prospective and retrospective observational studies, registries, postmarketing safety and effectiveness studies, pragmatic studies and long-term follow-up. Working with Business Development, Medical, Epidemiology, Biostatistics and other functional leaders, the Director translates evidence needs into feasible study plans, budgets and delivery commitments. The role is accountable for customer satisfaction, study and portfolio performance, and the development of assigned teams.

Strategy and customer engagement

Lead strategy for assigned RWLP opportunities, aligning customer evidence needs with study design, data availability, country requirements, operational feasibility and budget.
Lead proposal development and writing and bid defense preparation, including delivery models, country and site strategy, staffing, assumptions, timelines, budgets and risk mitigation. Coach team members to present their expertise and proposed solutions clearly.
Partner with Business Development and account leaders to develop customer relationships, identify follow-on opportunities and demonstrate RWLP capabilities through credible delivery commitments.
Ensure an effective transition from proposal to delivery, with clear ownership of commitments, assumptions, scope, resources and customer expectations.

RWLP study design and delivery

Apply working knowledge of interventional and non-interventional study designs, including cohort, case-control and cross-sectional studies; prospective and retrospective registries; chart reviews; pragmatic trials; postmarketing studies; and extension or long-term follow-up programs.
Partner with Epidemiology, Biostatistics and Medical to assess whether proposed populations, endpoints, follow-up schedules and data sources can answer the study objectives. Translate scientific recommendations into operational plans without substituting for specialist scientific accountability.
Assess delivery options using primary data collection, secondary data sources or a combination of both, including electronic health records, claims and existing registries. Identify data access, completeness, linkage, consent and site-workflow requirements with the relevant specialists.
Oversee feasibility, country and site selection, startup, recruitment, retention, monitoring, data collection and closeout. Adapt delivery to routine care and site capabilities while meeting protocol and applicable quality requirements.
Ensure monitoring and oversight are proportionate to study design, data risks and applicable requirements. Coordinate safety reporting, vendor oversight and event adjudication where required by the protocol.
Oversee assigned studies and portfolios against scope, timeline, quality and financial commitments. Review performance trends, resolve escalations and lead recovery plans with clear owners and deadlines.

Operational leadership and people management

Lead portfolio reviews and governance discussions; identify recurring delivery issues, capacity constraints and opportunities to improve execution across studies.
Partner with functional and resource leaders to forecast demand, allocate staff and balance workload, skills, continuity and cost across the assigned portfolio.
Provide line management for designated employees where assigned, including recruitment, onboarding, objective setting, coaching, performance reviews, development planning and succession planning.
Assess employee readiness for assigned responsibilities, identify training needs and oversee project handovers and role transitions. Address performance concerns with HR and the appropriate functional leaders.
Develop project leaders and cross-functional teams, clarify accountability and promote consistent delivery practices. Maintain defined decision rights with the ODL and functional leadership under the approved operating model.

Financial performance, quality and compliance

Own financial oversight for assigned studies and programs, including budget review, forecasting, resource utilization, profitability, scope management and timely change orders. Resolve variances with project teams and Finance.
Apply Good Pharmacoepidemiology Practices (GPP), Good Clinical Practice (GCP) and applicable local requirements according to study classification and activities. Work with Regulatory and Quality to confirm the appropriate framework.
Ensure compliance with company procedures, contractual commitments and applicable customer requirements. Coordinate ethics review, informed consent or approved waivers, privacy and data governance requirements with the responsible functions.
Maintain oversight of quality risks, deviations and corrective and preventive actions; support audit and inspection readiness and timely resolution of findings.
Use delivery metrics, customer feedback and lessons learned to improve RWLP processes, proposal assumptions, budget models and execution.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in life sciences, nursing, public health, epidemiology or a related discipline, or equivalent education and related experience. An advanced relevant degree is preferred.
Extensive relevant research experience within a CRO, pharmaceutical, biotechnology or comparable research organization, including demonstrated leadership of RWLP programs. Direct experience delivering both non-interventional and interventional late-phase studies is required.
Demonstrated understanding of observational and interventional study designs, routine-care research, primary and secondary data collection, and their operational implications.
Working knowledge of GPP, GCP and applicable global and local requirements for late-phase and non-interventional research, with the ability to apply the appropriate framework with specialist support.
Proven experience leading proposals, bid defenses and senior customer discussions, and translating evidence objectives into feasible, appropriately costed delivery plans.
Demonstrated portfolio or multi-study oversight, operational problem-solving, financial forecasting, resource planning and scope management.
Experience developing staff and leading cross-functional teams. Direct people-management experience is required where the role includes line-management accountability.
Ability to work effectively with Medical, Epidemiology, Biostatistics, Regulatory, Safety, Data Management and technology partners; sufficient therapeutic-area knowledge to lead credible customer discussions and identify when specialist input is needed.
Strong communication, presentation, negotiation and decision-making skills; ability to manage competing priorities and resolve issues with senior stakeholders.
Proficiency in core business and project-management tools; fluency in English; willingness to travel approximately 25%, consistent with business needs.

Critical Skills

RWLP strategy and delivery; study-design literacy; customer engagement; bid defense leadership; portfolio oversight; people development; resource planning; financial management; risk-based quality oversight; cross-functional decision-making.

US Experience Requirements

At least eight years of relevant research experience, including at least seven years managing studies, with demonstrated experience leading RWLP programs across interventional and non-interventional research.

Disclaimer

Tasks, duties, and responsibilities as listed in this job description are not exhaustive. The Company, at its sole discretion and with no prior notice, may assign other tasks, duties, and job responsibilities. Equivalent experience, skills, and/or education will also be considered so qualifications of incumbents may differ from those listed in the Job Description. The Company, at its sole discretion, will determine what constitutes as equivalent to the qualifications described above. Further, nothing contained herein should be construed to create an employment contract. Occasionally, required skills/experiences for jobs are expressed in brief terms. Any language contained herein is intended to fully comply with all obligations imposed by the legislation of each country in which it operates, including the implementation of the EU Equality Directive, in relation to the recruitment and employment of its employees. The Company is committed to compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act, including the provision of reasonable accommodations, when appropriate, to assist employees or applicants to perform the essential functions of the job.

US Physical Requirements and Work Environment

Physical Requirements: Position requires: ability to occasionally move about inside the office to access filing cabinets, office equipment, etc. and to move between office locations; ability to maintain a stationary position for prolonged periods of time; ability to occasionally manipulate (e.g., lift, carry, move) office items and packages of light to medium weights of 10-35 pounds; ability to constantly operate a computer and other office productivity equipment (e.g., scanner, phone, printer, copier); ability to perceive and assess written materials for prolonged periods of time; and ability to frequently communicate with colleagues on the phone, by email, and in-person. Work Environment: This job operates in a professional office environment. This role routinely uses standard office equipment such as computers, phones, photocopiers, and filing cabinets. The noise level in the work environment is low.

jobs.title: Vice President, Enterprise Services
jobs.location: St John’s, Newfoundland and Labrador, Canada
jobs.description:
WorkplaceNL
administers Newfoundland and Labrador’s mandatory, no-fault workplace injury compensation system, funded by employer assessments and investment returns. We promote safe workplaces and provide benefits and services to injured workers, helping improve quality of life across the province.

Overview

Reporting to the Chief Executive Officer, the Vice President, Enterprise Services brings an organization-wide perspective to strategy, performance, technology, people and enterprise risk.
This position provides executive leadership and strategic direction for Enterprise Services and is integral to WorkplaceNL’s modernization agenda, working in partnership with those leading transformation initiatives to ensure improvements are effectively integrated into ongoing operations. This is a long term temporary position, anticipated to span several years while WorkplaceNL advances its transformation and modernization program.

As a member of the Executive Team, you will help set WorkplaceNL’s direction and align people, resources and investments behind shared priorities. Your mandate extends beyond leading your portfolio: you will work across organizational boundaries, navigate competing needs and build support for changes that strengthen services and organizational performance.

You will also lead the continued development of WorkplaceNL’s Enterprise Risk Management Framework and report to the Board’s Governance Committee.

Responsibilities include but are not limited to:

Strategy and planning:
Working with the Executive Team and senior leaders to translate long-term priorities into evidence-based, multi-year plans with clear accountabilities and measurable outcomes.

Technology and information management:
Guiding technology investments, budgets and service delivery to support organizational priorities. Overseeing information management, cybersecurity and business resilience, and advising senior leaders and the Board on technology opportunities and risks.

Performance and improvement:
Leading corporate performance measurement, reporting and continuous improvement. Overseeing Internal Review, program evaluation and quality assurance, and guiding compliance with the Transparency and Accountability Act, annual performance reporting and CEO performance contracts.

Policy and government relations:
Guiding the policy framework and annual policy plan, overseeing statutory reviews and legislative priorities, and maintaining productive relationships with government and other stakeholders.

People and culture:
Setting the context for HR strategies that support employee health and safety, engagement, recruitment, retention and succession. Working with leaders to strengthen organizational capability and foster an ethical, inclusive and accountable workplace.

Enterprise risk:
Strengthening risk management across the organization, ensuring risks inform planning, investment and operational decisions, with clear reporting to the Executive Team and Board.

Who you are

You lead with an enterprise perspective, making decisions based on what serves the organization as a whole. You build trust across functions and understand the people dynamics that shape organizational performance. You can surface competing interests, work through disagreement and bring people together around a clear direction. Where delivery relies on shared resources, you help leaders make sound trade-offs, establish priorities and agree on how work will move forward.
You are comfortable leading change and transformation through influence, ingenuity as well as authority. You communicate the reasons for change clearly, build commitment and maintain accountability for results. You develop strong leaders, address concerns directly and create the conditions for teams to work effectively together.

You bring sound judgement and executive presence to discussions with the CEO, Board, government, and other stakeholders. You can explain complex issues clearly, offer candid advice and connect operational decisions to strategy, risk, financial stewardship and client service.

What you bring:

A university degree in business, public administration, humanities, science or relevant disciplines. A master’s degree in a relevant discipline would be considered an asset.
Minimum of ten years of progressive management experience in a public or private organization leading multiple lines of business and providing services to diverse client groups.
Demonstrated ability to navigate a public sector environment, balancing government priorities, board oversight, public accountability and organizational objectives.
Strong leadership abilities with exceptional interpersonal and communication skills and a proven track record of building effective stakeholder relationships.
Experience conceptualizing and executing strategies that advance cross-organizational priorities, including in the areas of information technology, data and analytics.
Experience applying best practices in enterprise risk management.
Experience with project planning, management and governance, especially as it relates to information technology.
Ability to think strategically, analytically, and use good judgement in providing oversight and solutions to corporate opportunities, challenges and risks.

Why Join Us?
Impactful work that contributes to the work safety in Newfoundland and Labrador.
Competitive base salary; range $126,040 - $163,852
Generous vacation and leave entitlements.
Comprehensive health and dental benefits.
Enrollment in the Public Service Pension Plan.
Opportunities for ongoing professional development.
A collaborative, supportive, and inclusive work environment.

At Workplace NL we are committed to workplace inclusion. Candidates of all backgrounds including but not limited to individuals with international experience, newcomers to Canada, women, Indigenous persons, persons with disabilities, members of visible minorities, and persons of various gender identities and sexual orientations are encouraged to apply. We welcome the opportunity to discuss accommodation at any point in the application process.

If you require reasonable accommodation to take part in the employment process, please call 709-437-4300 or send an email to recruitment@ethree.ca and let us know the nature of your request.
We thank all applicants for their interest. However, only those selected for an interview will be contacted.

jobs.title: Director, Patient Access & Channel Strategy
jobs.description:
Aperçu

Build the connections that bring innovation to patients.

Scientific progress creates possibilities. Helping patients access treatment takes people who can connect the dots—between support programs, reimbursement, pharmacies and the partners who deliver medicines.

At Incyte Canada, we are looking for an Associate Director / Director, Patient Access & Channel Strategy to strengthen those connections across oncology, hematology, immunology and dermatology. As our portfolio evolves and we prepare for upcoming launches, you will shape how patients access our therapies, building the programs, partnerships and capabilities to support them.

Patient Support Programs will be at the heart of your mandate. You will lead their strategy and delivery, strengthen our distribution partnerships and develop our pharmacy and channel approach. Working closely with colleagues across Market Access, Medical, Finance and Legal, you will turn complex challenges into practical solutions, combining strategic vision with the willingness to get into the detail and make things work.

We are looking for a builder, a thoughtful negotiator and a relationship leader. Someone who brings structure to ambiguity, earns trust across a complex healthcare ecosystem and takes ownership from strategy through execution.

An opportunity to shape a critical capability for Incyte Canada, and help patients access the innovation we work to deliver.

The Associate Director/Director, Patient Access & Channel Strategy is responsible for the strategic leadership, development, and execution of best-in-class Patient Support Programs (PSPs), trade relations, supply chain, and pharmacy/channel strategy supporting Incyte Canada's oncology/hematology and immunology/dermatology portfolio.

This role oversees a complex ecosystem of PSPs, vendors, wholesalers, distribution partners, pharmacies, and Group Purchasing Organizations (GPOs), ensuring seamless patient access to innovative therapies. The incumbent serves as the primary point of contact for Supply Chain within Canada, acts as the Quality Assurance (QA) Ambassador for the affiliate, and represents the organization externally with the Health Products Stewardship Association (HPSA).

In addition, the incumbent holds accountability for budget oversight and financial governance across PSP, trade, and channel-related activities. Working cross-functionally with Government Affairs, HEOR/Reimbursement Strategy, Private Insurance, Medical, Legal, Finance, and other key stakeholders, the incumbent drives operational excellence, compliance, and continuous improvement while delivering patient-centric solutions at scale.

Reporting to the Senior Director, Market Access & Government Affairs, this position will be filled at the Associate Director or Director level depending on the successful candidate's experience and demonstrated readiness for the full scope of commercial, pharmacy, and GPO responsibilities described below.

Essential Functions Of The Job (Key Responsibilities)

Patient Support Program Leadership (Primary Focus)
Own PSP strategy, performance, and day-to-day program integrity across the oncology/hematology and immunology/dermatology portfolios
Scale and adapt PSPs ahead of anticipated public reimbursement wins and upcoming launches
Set and monitor KPIs for program effectiveness, patient outcomes, and vendor performance; lead vendor selection, onboarding, and governance
Act as Incyte Canada’s internal Quality Assurance (QA) Ambassador for PSP operations — overseeing SOP adherence, supporting inspection readiness, and championing continuous improvement across vendor-delivered programs

Channel Strategy & Innovation

Build a multi-year channel and PSP strategy roadmap aligned to portfolio evolution
Continue to assess and refine the foundational infrastructure (governance, SOPs, vendor framework, KPIs)
Develop and maintain the business case for additional headcount and/or ongoing vendor support as scope is validated; lead hiring/onboarding as resources are approved

Cross-Functional Integration

Partner with Government Affairs, HEOR/Reimbursement Strategy, and the Private Insurance lead to ensure channel, trade, and pharmacy strategy reflects and reinforces active pCPA negotiations, CDA-AMC/INESSS outcomes, and payer strategy
Partner with Medical for Real World Evidence (RWE) generation
Provide a channel/trade lens into pricing and contracting strategy for both in-line and pipeline assets

Financial & Vendor Governance

Own PSP, trade, and channel-related budgets; manage forecasts, variance, and ROI reporting in partnership with Finance
Ensure cost-effective, compliant vendor management across PSP, trade, and GPO/pharmacy relationships, including short-term external vendor/agency engagements where internal capacity is still being built
Trade Relations & Supply Chain (Outsourced Vendor Management)
Own wholesaler and distribution partner relationships and commercial agreements
Negotiate and renew trade terms, ensuring uninterrupted product flow for publicly reimbursed, privately reimbursed, and pCPA-negotiated brands
Serve as the primary point of contact for Supply Chain in Canada; oversee 3PL operations, forecasting, and distribution planning
Where internal capacity is constrained, engage and manage external vendors/agencies to maintain trade and supply chain continuity
Serve as Incyte Canada’s liaison to the Health Products Stewardship Association (HPSA), ensuring compliance with environmental stewardship and product-return obligations tied to the wholesaler and distribution network
Pharmacy Strategy & Group Purchasing Organizations (As Strategic Build-Out)
Develop and execute Incyte Canada's pharmacy channel strategy across retail, specialty, and hospital pharmacy
Build and manage relationships with relevant GPOs and hospital shared-services organizations, prioritized around hospital-administered/infused oncology products and pipeline
Lead GPO and hospital contract negotiations in partnership with Legal and Finance, ensuring alignment with PMPRB pricing rules, the Competition Act, and Incyte's compliance framework
Assess buy-and-bill vs. PSP-mediated distribution models for infused and hospital-administered assets as they approach launch
Coordinate with the Private Insurance lead where pharmacy/specialty network strategy intersects with private payer plan design

Qualifications (Education, Experience & Competencies)

Education & Experience

Bachelor's degree in Life Sciences, Business, or related field; advanced degree an asset
Significant pharmaceutical/biotech experience leading Patient Support Programs at scale
Experience in trade relations, wholesaler management, and Canadian pharmaceutical distribution/supply chain
Experience with pharmacy channel strategy and/or GPO negotiation strongly preferred, ideally including hospital-administered or infused specialty products and buy-and-bill models
Working knowledge of Canadian public (CDA-AMC, INESSS, pCPA, PMPRB) and private reimbursement frameworks
Experience managing external vendors/agencies as an extension of a lean internal team; prior people-leadership experience, or demonstrated readiness to build and lead a team, considered an asset

Core Competencies

Program management rigor, particularly for PSP operations at scale
Commercial negotiation skill, with wholesalers, GPO/hospital counterparts, and vendors
Ability to operate with significant ambiguity, sequence competing priorities, and build structure from a limited existing foundation
Vendor and cross-functional stakeholder management, including managing agency/vendor resources as short-term capacity
Compliance and risk-awareness in a regulated, PMPRB-governed pricing environment
Collaborative mindset — able to identify and act on synergies with adjacent Market Access functions (e.g., Private Insurance)

Additional Requirements

Bilingualism (French and English) considered an asset.

Disclaimer

The above statements describe the general nature and level of work performed and are not intended to be an exhaustive list of all responsibilities, duties, or skills required. Management reserves the right to modify the role as needed.

Résumé du poste (fonction principale)

Le/la directeur(trice) associé(e)/directeur(trice), Accès aux patients et stratégie des canaux, est responsable de la direction stratégique, du développement et de la mise en œuvre de programmes de soutien aux patients (PSP), de relations commerciales, de chaîne d’approvisionnement et de stratégies pharmaceutiques et de canaux de distribution de premier ordre, soutenant le portefeuille d’oncologie/hématologie et d’immunologie/dermatologie d’Incyte Canada.

Ce poste supervise un écosystème complexe comprenant des PSP, des fournisseurs, des grossistes, des partenaires de distribution, des pharmacies et des organismes d’achats groupés (GPO), afin d’assurer un accès fluide des patients aux thérapies innovantes. Le titulaire agit à titre de principal point de contact pour la chaîne d’approvisionnement au Canada, assume le rôle d’ambassadeur de l’assurance qualité (AQ) pour la filiale et représente l’organisation à l’externe auprès de la Health Products Stewardship Association (HPSA).

De plus, le titulaire est responsable de la supervision budgétaire et de la gouvernance financière des activités liées aux PSP, aux relations commerciales et aux canaux de distribution. En collaboration étroite avec les équipes des Affaires gouvernementales, de l’HEOR/Stratégie de remboursement, de l’Assurance privée, des Affaires médicales, des Affaires juridiques, des Finances et d’autres parties prenantes clés, il favorise l’excellence opérationnelle, la conformité réglementaire et l’amélioration continue tout en offrant des solutions axées sur les patients à grande échelle.

Relevant du/de la directeur(trice) principal(e), Accès au marché et Affaires gouvernementales, ce poste sera pourvu au niveau directeur(trice) associé(e) ou directeur(trice), selon l’expérience du/de la candidat(e) retenu(e) et sa capacité démontrée à assumer l’ensemble des responsabilités commerciales, pharmaceutiques et liées aux GPO décrites ci-dessous.

Fonctions essentielles du poste (principales responsabilités)

Leadership des programmes de soutien aux patients (principal domaine d’activité)
Assurer la responsabilité de la stratégie PSP, de la performance et de l’intégrité opérationnelle quotidienne des programmes dans les portefeuilles d’oncologie/hématologie et d’immunologie/dermatologie.
Développer et adapter les PSP en prévision des gains attendus en matière de remboursement public et des lancements à venir.
Définir et suivre les indicateurs clés de performance (KPI) liés à l’efficacité des programmes, aux résultats pour les patients et à la performance des fournisseurs; diriger la sélection, l’intégration et la gouvernance des fournisseurs.
Agir à titre d’ambassadeur interne de l’assurance qualité (AQ) d’Incyte Canada pour les opérations PSP, notamment en supervisant le respect des procédures opérationnelles normalisées (SOP), en soutenant la préparation aux inspections et en favorisant l’amélioration continue des programmes gérés par des fournisseurs.

Stratégie de canaux et innovation

Élaborer une feuille de route pluriannuelle pour les stratégies de canaux et de PSP, alignée sur l’évolution du portefeuille.
Évaluer et optimiser continuellement l’infrastructure de base (gouvernance, SOP, cadre de gestion des fournisseurs, KPI).
Élaborer et maintenir l’analyse de rentabilisation pour l’ajout de ressources internes et/ou le soutien continu de fournisseurs externes à mesure que les besoins sont validés; diriger le recrutement et l’intégration lorsque les ressources sont approuvées.

Intégration interfonctionnelle

Collaborer avec les équipes des Affaires gouvernementales, de l’HEOR/Stratégie de remboursement et de l’Assurance privée afin de garantir que les stratégies de canaux, commerciales et pharmaceutiques reflètent et soutiennent

The incumbent serves as the primary point of contact for Supply Chain within Canada, acts as the Quality Assurance (QA) Ambassador for the affiliate, and represents the organization externally with the Health Products Stewardship Association (HPSA).

In addition, the incumbent holds accountability for budget oversight and financial governance across PSP, trade, and channel-related activities. Working cross-functionally with Government Affairs, HEOR/Reimbursement Strategy, Private Insurance, Medical, Legal, Finance, and other key stakeholders, the incumbent drives operational excellence, compliance, and continuous improvement while delivering patient-centric solutions at scale.

Reporting to the Senior Director, Market Access & Government Affairs, this position will be filled at the Associate Director or Director level depending on the successful candidate's experience and demonstrated readiness for the full scope of commercial, pharmacy, and GPO responsibilities described below.

Essential Functions Of The Job (Key Responsibilities)

Patient Support Program Leadership (Primary Focus)
Own PSP strategy, performance, and day-to-day program integrity across the oncology/hematology and immunology/dermatology portfolios
Scale and adapt PSPs ahead of anticipated public reimbursement wins and upcoming launches
Set and monitor KPIs for program effectiveness, patient outcomes, and vendor performance; lead vendor selection, onboarding, and governance
Act as Incyte Canada’s internal Quality Assurance (QA) Ambassador for PSP operations — overseeing SOP adherence, supporting inspection readiness, and championing continuous improvement across vendor-delivered programs

Channel Strategy & Innovation

Build a multi-year channel and PSP strategy roadmap aligned to portfolio evolution
Continue to assess and refine the foundational infrastructure (governance, SOPs, vendor framework, KPIs)
Develop and maintain the business case for additional headcount and/or ongoing vendor support as scope is validated; lead hiring/onboarding as resources are approved

Cross-Functional Integration

Partner with Government Affairs, HEOR/Reimbursement Strategy, and the Private Insurance lead to ensure channel, trade, and pharmacy strategy reflects and reinforces active pCPA negotiations, CDA-AMC/INESSS outcomes, and payer strategy
Partner with Medical for Real World Evidence (RWE) generation
Provide a channel/trade lens into pricing and contracting strategy for both in-line and pipeline assets

Financial & Vendor Governance

Own PSP, trade, and channel-related budgets; manage forecasts, variance, and ROI reporting in partnership with Finance
Ensure cost-effective, compliant vendor management across PSP, trade, and GPO/pharmacy relationships, including short-term external vendor/agency engagements where internal capacity is still being built
Trade Relations & Supply Chain (Outsourced Vendor Management)
Own wholesaler and distribution partner relationships and commercial agreements
Negotiate and renew trade terms, ensuring uninterrupted product flow for publicly reimbursed, privately reimbursed, and pCPA-negotiated brands
Serve as the primary point of contact for Supply Chain in Canada; oversee 3PL operations, forecasting, and distribution planning
Where internal capacity is constrained, engage and manage external vendors/agencies to maintain trade and supply chain continuity
Serve as Incyte Canada’s liaison to the Health Products Stewardship Association (HPSA), ensuring compliance with environmental stewardship and product-return obligations tied to the wholesaler and distribution network
Pharmacy Strategy & Group Purchasing Organizations (As Strategic Build-Out)
Develop and execute Incyte Canada's pharmacy channel strategy across retail, specialty, and hospital pharmacy
Build and manage relationships with relevant GPOs and hospital shared-services organizations, prioritized around hospital-administered/infused oncology products and pipeline
Lead GPO and hospital contract negotiations in partnership with Legal and Finance, ensuring alignment with PMPRB pricing rules, the Competition Act, and Incyte's compliance framework
Assess buy-and-bill vs. PSP-mediated distribution models for infused and hospital-administered assets as they approach launch
Coordinate with the Private Insurance lead where pharmacy/specialty network strategy intersects with private payer plan design

Qualifications (Education, Experience & Competencies)

Education & Experience

Bachelor's degree in Life Sciences, Business, or related field; advanced degree an asset
Significant pharmaceutical/biotech experience leading Patient Support Programs at scale
Experience in trade relations, wholesaler management, and Canadian pharmaceutical distribution/supply chain
Experience with pharmacy channel strategy and/or GPO negotiation strongly preferred, ideally including hospital-administered or infused specialty products and buy-and-bill models
Working knowledge of Canadian public (CDA-AMC, INESSS, pCPA, PMPRB) and private reimbursement frameworks
Experience managing external vendors/agencies as an extension of a lean internal team; prior people-leadership experience, or demonstrated readiness to build and lead a team, considered an asset

Core Competencies

Program management rigor, particularly for PSP operations at scale
Commercial negotiation skill, with wholesalers, GPO/hospital counterparts, and vendors
Ability to operate with significant ambiguity, sequence competing priorities, and build structure from a limited existing foundation
Vendor and cross-functional stakeholder management, including managing agency/vendor resources as short-term capacity
Compliance and risk-awareness in a regulated, PMPRB-governed pricing environment
Collaborative mindset — able to identify and act on synergies with adjacent Market Access functions (e.g., Private Insurance)

Additional Requirements

Bilingualism (French and English) considered an asset.

Disclaimer

The above statements describe the general nature and level of work performed and are not intended to be an exhaustive list of all responsibilities, duties, or skills required. Management reserves the right to modify the role as needed.

Résumé du poste (fonction principale)

Le/la directeur(trice) associé(e)/directeur(trice), Accès aux patients et stratégie des canaux, est responsable de la direction stratégique, du développement et de la mise en œuvre de programmes de soutien aux patients (PSP), de relations commerciales, de chaîne d’approvisionnement et de stratégies pharmaceutiques et de canaux de distribution de premier ordre, soutenant le portefeuille d’oncologie/hématologie et d’immunologie/dermatologie d’Incyte Canada.

Ce poste supervise un écosystème complexe comprenant des PSP, des fournisseurs, des grossistes, des partenaires de distribution, des pharmacies et des organismes d’achats groupés (GPO), afin d’assurer un accès fluide des patients aux thérapies innovantes. Le titulaire agit à titre de principal point de contact pour la chaîne d’approvisionnement au Canada, assume le rôle d’ambassadeur de l’assurance qualité (AQ) pour la filiale et représente l’organisation à l’externe auprès de la Health Products Stewardship Association (HPSA).

De plus, le titulaire est responsable de la supervision budgétaire et de la gouvernance financière des activités liées aux PSP, aux relations commerciales et aux canaux de distribution. En collaboration étroite avec les équipes des Affaires gouvernementales, de l’HEOR/Stratégie de remboursement, de l’Assurance privée, des Affaires médicales, des Affaires juridiques, des Finances et d’autres parties prenantes clés, il favorise l’excellence opérationnelle, la conformité réglementaire et l’amélioration continue tout en offrant des solutions axées sur les patients à grande échelle.

Relevant du/de la directeur(trice) principal(e), Accès au marché et Affaires gouvernementales, ce poste sera pourvu au niveau directeur(trice) associé(e) ou directeur(trice), selon l’expérience du/de la candidat(e) retenu(e) et sa capacité démontrée à assumer l’ensemble des responsabilités commerciales, pharmaceutiques et liées aux GPO décrites ci-dessous.

Fonctions essentielles du poste (principales responsabilités)

Leadership des programmes de soutien aux patients (principal domaine d’activité)
Assurer la responsabilité de la stratégie PSP, de la performance et de l’intégrité opérationnelle quotidienne des programmes dans les portefeuilles d’oncologie/hématologie et d’immunologie/dermatologie.
Développer et adapter les PSP en prévision des gains attendus en matière de remboursement public et des lancements à venir.
Définir et suivre les indicateurs clés de performance (KPI) liés à l’efficacité des programmes, aux résultats pour les patients et à la performance des fournisseurs; diriger la sélection, l’intégration et la gouvernance des fournisseurs.
Agir à titre d’ambassadeur interne de l’assurance qualité (AQ) d’Incyte Canada pour les opérations PSP, notamment en supervisant le respect des procédures opérationnelles normalisées (SOP), en soutenant la préparation aux inspections et en favorisant l’amélioration continue des programmes gérés par des fournisseurs.

Stratégie de canaux et innovation

Élaborer une feuille de route pluriannuelle pour les stratégies de canaux et de PSP, alignée sur l’évolution du portefeuille.
Évaluer et optimiser continuellement l’infrastructure de base (gouvernance, SOP, cadre de gestion des fournisseurs, KPI).
Élaborer et maintenir l’analyse de rentabilisation pour l’ajout de ressources internes et/ou le soutien continu de fournisseurs externes à mesure que les besoins sont validés; diriger le recrutement et l’intégration lorsque les ressources sont approuvées.

Intégration interfonctionnelle

Collaborer avec les équipes des Affaires gouvernementales, de l’HEOR/Stratégie de remboursement et de l’Assurance privée afin de garantir que les stratégies de canaux, commerciales et pharmaceutiques reflètent et soutiennent

Build the connections that bring innovation to patients.

Scientific progress creates possibilities. Helping patients access treatment takes people who can connect the dots—between support programs, reimbursement, pharmacies and the partners who deliver medicines.

At Incyte Canada, we are looking for an Associate Director / Director, Patient Access & Channel Strategy to strengthen those connections across oncology, hematology, immunology and dermatology. As our portfolio evolves and we prepare for upcoming launches, you will shape how patients access our therapies, building the programs, partnerships and capabilities to support them.

Patient Support Programs will be at the heart of your mandate. You will lead their strategy and delivery, strengthen our distribution partnerships and develop our pharmacy and channel approach. Working closely with colleagues across Market Access, Medical, Finance and Legal, you will turn complex challenges into practical solutions, combining strategic vision with the willingness to get into the detail and make things work.

We are looking for a builder, a thoughtful negotiator and a relationship leader. Someone who brings structure to ambiguity, earns trust across a complex healthcare ecosystem and takes ownership from strategy through execution.

An opportunity to shape a critical capability for Incyte Canada, and help patients access the innovation we work to deliver.

jobs.description:
Additional Information

Job Number
26144079

Event Management

209 Fourth Avenue SE, 0, Calgary AB T2G 0C6, Canada VIEW ON MAP

Schedule
Full Time

Located Remotely?
N

Management

Bonus Eligible:
Y

Job Summary

Manages event management functions and staff on a daily basis, including the departments of Event Planning, Banquets/Catering, Event Service and Event Technology (Destination Management, if applicable). Position has overall responsibility for executing all property events with a seamless turnover from sales to operations and back to sales while consistently delivering a high level of service. Ensures team maximizes revenue opportunities by up-selling and accurately forecasting (catering and group rooms) all events. The position is responsible for achieving guest and employee satisfaction and for managing the financial performance of the department.

CANDIDATE PROFILE

Education And Experience

High school diploma or GED; 4 years experience in the event management, food and beverage, sales and marketing, or related professional area.

OR

2-year degree from an accredited university in Hotel and Restaurant Management, Hospitality, Business Administration, or related major; 2 years experience in the event management, food and beverage, sales and marketing, or related professional area.

CORE WORK ACTIVITIES

Managing Event Planning Operations

Leads execution of activities to support the Event Management strategy.
Works with direct reports to review scheduled events and event complexity in order to avoid potential service challenges and failures.
Ensures the property is apprised of all groups that will impact property operations.
Ensures meeting space and corresponding heart of the house areas are cleaned and maintained.
Ensures furniture and equipment is maintained and inventory levels are kept in accordance to corporate guidelines.
Leads the catering menu development process.
Works with culinary team to ensure compliance to food handling and sanitation standards.
Oversees turned opportunities’ function space and group room blocks.
Maintains inventories to maximize customer satisfaction and revenue opportunities.
Communicates and executes departmental and property emergency procedures and ensures staff are trained in safety procedures.
Reviews property specific event operations annually and makes appropriate adjustments.
Consult with customers in order to determine objectives and requirements for events such as meetings, conferences, and conventions.
Works directly with high profile and high revenue groups to ensure an excellent customer experience for all customers.

Leading Discipline and Department Teams

Displays leadership in guest hospitality, exemplifies excellent customer service and creates a positive atmosphere for guest relations.
Communicates vision for service delivery in Event Management to ensure guest is serviced from arrival to departure (e.g., greeting from maitre’d or event services team, food and beverage delivery, fulfillment of special requests, invitation to return).
Assigns all events turned over to Event Planning team (if no DEP).
Manages customer budgets to maximize revenue and meet customer needs.
Champions all standards, policies and procedures (PPM, Core Deliverables, SOPs, LSOPs, etc.).

Ensuring and Providing Exceptional Customer Service

Interacts with guests to obtain feedback on product quality and service levels.
Responds to and handles guest problems and complaints.
Empowers employees to provide excellent customer service.
Establishes guidelines so employees understand expectations and parameters.

Managing the Sales and Marketing Strategy

Develops working relationships with outside vendors and establishes prices and service agreements to enhance the event experience and to increase additional revenue opportunities for the property.

Conducting Human Resources Activities

Works with Human Resources to ensure compliance with all applicable laws and regulations.
Ensures that regular, ongoing communication is happening in all areas of event operations (e.g., Banquet Event Order meetings, pre-event briefings and staff meetings).
Reviews staffing levels to ensure that guest service and operational needs are met.

new_jobs.title: Vice President, Enterprise Services
new_jobs.location: St John’s, Newfoundland and Labrador, Canada
new_jobs.description:
WorkplaceNL
administers Newfoundland and Labrador’s mandatory, no-fault workplace injury compensation system, funded by employer assessments and investment returns. We promote safe workplaces and provide benefits and services to injured workers, helping improve quality of life across the province.

Overview

Reporting to the Chief Executive Officer, the Vice President, Enterprise Services brings an organization-wide perspective to strategy, performance, technology, people and enterprise risk.
This position provides executive leadership and strategic direction for Enterprise Services and is integral to WorkplaceNL’s modernization agenda, working in partnership with those leading transformation initiatives to ensure improvements are effectively integrated into ongoing operations. This is a long term temporary position, anticipated to span several years while WorkplaceNL advances its transformation and modernization program.

As a member of the Executive Team, you will help set WorkplaceNL’s direction and align people, resources and investments behind shared priorities. Your mandate extends beyond leading your portfolio: you will work across organizational boundaries, navigate competing needs and build support for changes that strengthen services and organizational performance.

You will also lead the continued development of WorkplaceNL’s Enterprise Risk Management Framework and report to the Board’s Governance Committee.

Responsibilities include but are not limited to:

Strategy and planning:
Working with the Executive Team and senior leaders to translate long-term priorities into evidence-based, multi-year plans with clear accountabilities and measurable outcomes.

Technology and information management:
Guiding technology investments, budgets and service delivery to support organizational priorities. Overseeing information management, cybersecurity and business resilience, and advising senior leaders and the Board on technology opportunities and risks.

Performance and improvement:
Leading corporate performance measurement, reporting and continuous improvement. Overseeing Internal Review, program evaluation and quality assurance, and guiding compliance with the Transparency and Accountability Act, annual performance reporting and CEO performance contracts.

Policy and government relations:
Guiding the policy framework and annual policy plan, overseeing statutory reviews and legislative priorities, and maintaining productive relationships with government and other stakeholders.

People and culture:
Setting the context for HR strategies that support employee health and safety, engagement, recruitment, retention and succession. Working with leaders to strengthen organizational capability and foster an ethical, inclusive and accountable workplace.

Enterprise risk:
Strengthening risk management across the organization, ensuring risks inform planning, investment and operational decisions, with clear reporting to the Executive Team and Board.

Who you are

You lead with an enterprise perspective, making decisions based on what serves the organization as a whole. You build trust across functions and understand the people dynamics that shape organizational performance. You can surface competing interests, work through disagreement and bring people together around a clear direction. Where delivery relies on shared resources, you help leaders make sound trade-offs, establish priorities and agree on how work will move forward.
You are comfortable leading change and transformation through influence, ingenuity as well as authority. You communicate the reasons for change clearly, build commitment and maintain accountability for results. You develop strong leaders, address concerns directly and create the conditions for teams to work effectively together.

You bring sound judgement and executive presence to discussions with the CEO, Board, government, and other stakeholders. You can explain complex issues clearly, offer candid advice and connect operational decisions to strategy, risk, financial stewardship and client service.

What you bring:

A university degree in business, public administration, humanities, science or relevant disciplines. A master’s degree in a relevant discipline would be considered an asset.
Minimum of ten years of progressive management experience in a public or private organization leading multiple lines of business and providing services to diverse client groups.
Demonstrated ability to navigate a public sector environment, balancing government priorities, board oversight, public accountability and organizational objectives.
Strong leadership abilities with exceptional interpersonal and communication skills and a proven track record of building effective stakeholder relationships.
Experience conceptualizing and executing strategies that advance cross-organizational priorities, including in the areas of information technology, data and analytics.
Experience applying best practices in enterprise risk management.
Experience with project planning, management and governance, especially as it relates to information technology.
Ability to think strategically, analytically, and use good judgement in providing oversight and solutions to corporate opportunities, challenges and risks.

Why Join Us?
Impactful work that contributes to the work safety in Newfoundland and Labrador.
Competitive base salary; range $126,040 - $163,852
Generous vacation and leave entitlements.
Comprehensive health and dental benefits.
Enrollment in the Public Service Pension Plan.
Opportunities for ongoing professional development.
A collaborative, supportive, and inclusive work environment.

At Workplace NL we are committed to workplace inclusion. Candidates of all backgrounds including but not limited to individuals with international experience, newcomers to Canada, women, Indigenous persons, persons with disabilities, members of visible minorities, and persons of various gender identities and sexual orientations are encouraged to apply. We welcome the opportunity to discuss accommodation at any point in the application process.

If you require reasonable accommodation to take part in the employment process, please call 709-437-4300 or send an email to recruitment@ethree.ca and let us know the nature of your request.
We thank all applicants for their interest. However, only those selected for an interview will be contacted.

Build the connections that bring innovation to patients.

Scientific progress creates possibilities. Helping patients access treatment takes people who can connect the dots—between support programs, reimbursement, pharmacies and the partners who deliver medicines.

At Incyte Canada, we are looking for an Associate Director / Director, Patient Access & Channel Strategy to strengthen those connections across oncology, hematology, immunology and dermatology. As our portfolio evolves and we prepare for upcoming launches, you will shape how patients access our therapies, building the programs, partnerships and capabilities to support them.

Patient Support Programs will be at the heart of your mandate. You will lead their strategy and delivery, strengthen our distribution partnerships and develop our pharmacy and channel approach. Working closely with colleagues across Market Access, Medical, Finance and Legal, you will turn complex challenges into practical solutions, combining strategic vision with the willingness to get into the detail and make things work.

We are looking for a builder, a thoughtful negotiator and a relationship leader. Someone who brings structure to ambiguity, earns trust across a complex healthcare ecosystem and takes ownership from strategy through execution.

An opportunity to shape a critical capability for Incyte Canada, and help patients access the innovation we work to deliver.

The Associate Director/Director, Patient Access & Channel Strategy is responsible for the strategic leadership, development, and execution of best-in-class Patient Support Programs (PSPs), trade relations, supply chain, and pharmacy/channel strategy supporting Incyte Canada's oncology/hematology and immunology/dermatology portfolio.

This role oversees a complex ecosystem of PSPs, vendors, wholesalers, distribution partners, pharmacies, and Group Purchasing Organizations (GPOs), ensuring seamless patient access to innovative therapies. The incumbent serves as the primary point of contact for Supply Chain within Canada, acts as the Quality Assurance (QA) Ambassador for the affiliate, and represents the organization externally with the Health Products Stewardship Association (HPSA).

In addition, the incumbent holds accountability for budget oversight and financial governance across PSP, trade, and channel-related activities. Working cross-functionally with Government Affairs, HEOR/Reimbursement Strategy, Private Insurance, Medical, Legal, Finance, and other key stakeholders, the incumbent drives operational excellence, compliance, and continuous improvement while delivering patient-centric solutions at scale.

Reporting to the Senior Director, Market Access & Government Affairs, this position will be filled at the Associate Director or Director level depending on the successful candidate's experience and demonstrated readiness for the full scope of commercial, pharmacy, and GPO responsibilities described below.

Essential Functions Of The Job (Key Responsibilities)

Patient Support Program Leadership (Primary Focus)
Own PSP strategy, performance, and day-to-day program integrity across the oncology/hematology and immunology/dermatology portfolios
Scale and adapt PSPs ahead of anticipated public reimbursement wins and upcoming launches
Set and monitor KPIs for program effectiveness, patient outcomes, and vendor performance; lead vendor selection, onboarding, and governance
Act as Incyte Canada’s internal Quality Assurance (QA) Ambassador for PSP operations — overseeing SOP adherence, supporting inspection readiness, and championing continuous improvement across vendor-delivered programs

Channel Strategy & Innovation

Build a multi-year channel and PSP strategy roadmap aligned to portfolio evolution
Continue to assess and refine the foundational infrastructure (governance, SOPs, vendor framework, KPIs)
Develop and maintain the business case for additional headcount and/or ongoing vendor support as scope is validated; lead hiring/onboarding as resources are approved

Cross-Functional Integration

Partner with Government Affairs, HEOR/Reimbursement Strategy, and the Private Insurance lead to ensure channel, trade, and pharmacy strategy reflects and reinforces active pCPA negotiations, CDA-AMC/INESSS outcomes, and payer strategy
Partner with Medical for Real World Evidence (RWE) generation
Provide a channel/trade lens into pricing and contracting strategy for both in-line and pipeline assets

Financial & Vendor Governance

Own PSP, trade, and channel-related budgets; manage forecasts, variance, and ROI reporting in partnership with Finance
Ensure cost-effective, compliant vendor management across PSP, trade, and GPO/pharmacy relationships, including short-term external vendor/agency engagements where internal capacity is still being built
Trade Relations & Supply Chain (Outsourced Vendor Management)
Own wholesaler and distribution partner relationships and commercial agreements
Negotiate and renew trade terms, ensuring uninterrupted product flow for publicly reimbursed, privately reimbursed, and pCPA-negotiated brands
Serve as the primary point of contact for Supply Chain in Canada; oversee 3PL operations, forecasting, and distribution planning
Where internal capacity is constrained, engage and manage external vendors/agencies to maintain trade and supply chain continuity
Serve as Incyte Canada’s liaison to the Health Products Stewardship Association (HPSA), ensuring compliance with environmental stewardship and product-return obligations tied to the wholesaler and distribution network
Pharmacy Strategy & Group Purchasing Organizations (As Strategic Build-Out)
Develop and execute Incyte Canada's pharmacy channel strategy across retail, specialty, and hospital pharmacy
Build and manage relationships with relevant GPOs and hospital shared-services organizations, prioritized around hospital-administered/infused oncology products and pipeline
Lead GPO and hospital contract negotiations in partnership with Legal and Finance, ensuring alignment with PMPRB pricing rules, the Competition Act, and Incyte's compliance framework
Assess buy-and-bill vs. PSP-mediated distribution models for infused and hospital-administered assets as they approach launch
Coordinate with the Private Insurance lead where pharmacy/specialty network strategy intersects with private payer plan design

Qualifications (Education, Experience & Competencies)

Education & Experience

Bachelor's degree in Life Sciences, Business, or related field; advanced degree an asset
Significant pharmaceutical/biotech experience leading Patient Support Programs at scale
Experience in trade relations, wholesaler management, and Canadian pharmaceutical distribution/supply chain
Experience with pharmacy channel strategy and/or GPO negotiation strongly preferred, ideally including hospital-administered or infused specialty products and buy-and-bill models
Working knowledge of Canadian public (CDA-AMC, INESSS, pCPA, PMPRB) and private reimbursement frameworks
Experience managing external vendors/agencies as an extension of a lean internal team; prior people-leadership experience, or demonstrated readiness to build and lead a team, considered an asset

Core Competencies

Program management rigor, particularly for PSP operations at scale
Commercial negotiation skill, with wholesalers, GPO/hospital counterparts, and vendors
Ability to operate with significant ambiguity, sequence competing priorities, and build structure from a limited existing foundation
Vendor and cross-functional stakeholder management, including managing agency/vendor resources as short-term capacity
Compliance and risk-awareness in a regulated, PMPRB-governed pricing environment
Collaborative mindset — able to identify and act on synergies with adjacent Market Access functions (e.g., Private Insurance)

Additional Requirements

Bilingualism (French and English) considered an asset.

Résumé du poste (fonction principale)

Le/la directeur(trice) associé(e)/directeur(trice), Accès aux patients et stratégie des canaux, est responsable de la direction stratégique, du développement et de la mise en œuvre de programmes de soutien aux patients (PSP), de relations commerciales, de chaîne d’approvisionnement et de stratégies pharmaceutiques et de canaux de distribution de premier ordre, soutenant le portefeuille d’oncologie/hématologie et d’immunologie/dermatologie d’Incyte Canada.

Ce poste supervise un écosystème complexe comprenant des PSP, des fournisseurs, des grossistes, des partenaires de distribution, des pharmacies et des organismes d’achats groupés (GPO), afin d’assurer un accès fluide des patients aux thérapies innovantes. Le titulaire agit à titre de principal point de contact pour la chaîne d’approvisionnement au Canada, assume le rôle d’ambassadeur de l’assurance qualité (AQ) pour la filiale et représente l’organisation à l’externe auprès de la Health Products Stewardship Association (HPSA).

De plus, le titulaire est responsable de la supervision budgétaire et de la gouvernance financière des activités liées aux PSP, aux relations commerciales et aux canaux de distribution. En collaboration étroite avec les équipes des Affaires gouvernementales, de l’HEOR/Stratégie de remboursement, de l’Assurance privée, des Affaires médicales, des Affaires juridiques, des Finances et d’autres parties prenantes clés, il favorise l’excellence opérationnelle, la conformité réglementaire et l’amélioration continue tout en offrant des solutions axées sur les patients à grande échelle.

Relevant du/de la directeur(trice) principal(e), Accès au marché et Affaires gouvernementales, ce poste sera pourvu au niveau directeur(trice) associé(e) ou directeur(trice), selon l’expérience du/de la candidat(e) retenu(e) et sa capacité démontrée à assumer l’ensemble des responsabilités commerciales, pharmaceutiques et liées aux GPO décrites ci-dessous.

Fonctions essentielles du poste (principales responsabilités)

Leadership des programmes de soutien aux patients (principal domaine d’activité)
Assurer la responsabilité de la stratégie PSP, de la performance et de l’intégrité opérationnelle quotidienne des programmes dans les portefeuilles d’oncologie/hématologie et d’immunologie/dermatologie.
Développer et adapter les PSP en prévision des gains attendus en matière de remboursement public et des lancements à venir.
Définir et suivre les indicateurs clés de performance (KPI) liés à l’efficacité des programmes, aux résultats pour les patients et à la performance des fournisseurs; diriger la sélection, l’intégration et la gouvernance des fournisseurs.
Agir à titre d’ambassadeur interne de l’assurance qualité (AQ) d’Incyte Canada pour les opérations PSP, notamment en supervisant le respect des procédures opérationnelles normalisées (SOP), en soutenant la préparation aux inspections et en favorisant l’amélioration continue des programmes gérés par des fournisseurs.

Stratégie de canaux et innovation

Élaborer une feuille de route pluriannuelle pour les stratégies de canaux et de PSP, alignée sur l’évolution du portefeuille.
Évaluer et optimiser continuellement l’infrastructure de base (gouvernance, SOP, cadre de gestion des fournisseurs, KPI).
Élaborer et maintenir l’analyse de rentabilisation pour l’ajout de ressources internes et/ou le soutien continu de fournisseurs externes à mesure que les besoins sont validés; diriger le recrutement et l’intégration lorsque les ressources sont approuvées.

Intégration interfonctionnelle

Collaborer avec les équipes des Affaires gouvernementales, de l’HEOR/Stratégie de remboursement et de l’Assurance privée afin de garantir que les stratégies de canaux, commerciales et pharmaceutiques reflètent et soutiennent
